challenges: sharding with consistent hashing or hash slots

resources.title: Google Docs System Design (Collaborative Editor)
challenges: merging concurrent edits with operational transform

resources.title: CDN System Design (Global Content Delivery Network)
HTTP
resources.description: How HTTP methods, status codes, cookies and caching behave, and what changed between HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

resources.title: DNS
resources.description: How a hostname is resolved through recursive lookups, and how record types, TTLs and caching influence failover and traffic distribution.

resources.title: TCP
resources.description: How a TCP connection is established, kept reliable under packet loss and congestion, and closed.

resources.title: Load Balancer
resources.description: How load balancers choose servers, detect unhealthy ones, drain connections and, in multi-region designs, fail over between regions.

resources.title: API Gateway
resources.description: What a single logical entry point adds to a service architecture: routing, authentication, rate limiting and aggregation.

resources.title: Reverse Proxy (Nginx)
resources.description: What a reverse proxy such as Nginx does in front of servers: TLS termination, routing, caching and availability.

resources.title: CDN Fundamentals
resources.description: How edge caches in a content delivery network (CDN) serve content near users, and how TTLs, invalidation and origin shielding shape hit rates.

resources.title: API Design
resources.description: How to design consistent API contracts, including resource modeling, error handling, pagination and versioning.

resources.title: REST APIs
resources.description: Which constraints make an API RESTful, how method semantics interact with caching, and how REST differs from RPC.

resources.title: gRPC
resources.description: How Protobuf contracts, streaming calls and deadlines work in gRPC, and when it is a better fit than REST.

resources.title: Pagination
resources.description: Why offset pagination slows on deep pages, how keyset pagination backed by an index reduces that scanning cost, and how concurrent changes affect page results.

resources.title: Idempotency
resources.description: How idempotency keys let clients retry safely, and how to handle concurrent duplicates and a reused key with a different payload.

resources.title: Database Foundations
resources.description: How databases store data, run queries, apply durability mechanisms such as logging, and coordinate concurrent access, with the limits of those guarantees, before you study indexing or transactions.

resources.title: Database Data Modeling
resources.description: How keys, constraints, normalization and query-driven design shape a schema, and techniques for migrating it while the system stays online.

resources.title: Database Indexing
resources.description: How indexes speed up queries, how composite indexes are ordered, and why the optimizer sometimes ignores an index.

resources.title: Database Transactions & Concurrency
resources.description: What ACID guarantees, isolation levels, locking and multi-version concurrency control (MVCC) mean, and when optimistic or pessimistic concurrency fits.

resources.title: Specialized Data Stores
resources.description: A comparison of relational, document, key-value, search, time-series, graph and vector databases, with guidance on matching each to a workload.

resources.title: PostgreSQL
resources.description: How PostgreSQL implements MVCC, indexing, query planning, write-ahead logging and streaming replication.

resources.title: MongoDB
resources.description: How MongoDB handles flexible schemas, aggregation, multi-document transactions, replication and sharding.

resources.title: Cassandra
resources.description: How Cassandra partitions and replicates data across a masterless cluster with tunable consistency, gossip and compaction.

resources.title: Elasticsearch
resources.description: How inverted indexes, relevance scoring and sharding enable near-real-time full-text search across a cluster.

resources.title: Database Scaling
resources.description: Compare query optimization, caching, read replicas and sharding, and recognize the bottlenecks and failure modes that make each one appropriate.

resources.title: Redis
resources.description: How Redis serves caching, sessions, streams and pub/sub from memory, and how persistence, replication and cluster sharding work.

resources.title: Consistent Hashing
resources.description: How consistent hashing limits key movement when nodes join or leave, and which problems it does not solve.

resources.title: Queues & Workers
resources.description: Explore queued execution, acknowledgement and redelivery, crashed-worker recovery, and the limits of delivery and processing guarantees.

resources.title: Pub/Sub
resources.description: How publish/subscribe fans events out to independent consumers, and how ordering scope, schema changes and, in some brokers, consumer groups behave.

resources.title: Job Processing
resources.description: How a background job moves through queued, running, retry and failed states, using leases, heartbeats and idempotency.

resources.title: Outbox Pattern
resources.description: Why writing to a database and publishing an event separately can lose one of them, how an outbox table closes that gap, and why consumers must still deduplicate.

resources.title: Dead-Letter Queues
resources.description: How dead-letter queues set aside unprocessable messages for inspection and replay, and why they do not replace a retry policy.

resources.title: Kafka
resources.description: Explore partitioned Kafka logs, replication and retention, then per-partition ordering, consumer group assignment, offset commits and recovery.

resources.title: RabbitMQ
resources.description: How RabbitMQ routes messages through exchanges and queues, and how acknowledgements, flow control and durability handle failures.

resources.title: Distributed Data and the CAP Theorem
resources.description: Reason about replication, partitioning and quorums, and the availability–consistency trade-off that CAP describes during a network partition.

resources.title: Distributed Locks
resources.description: How leases, TTLs and fencing tokens make distributed locks safer, and when a lock is the wrong tool.

resources.title: Saga Pattern
resources.description: How sagas coordinate a multi-service transaction with compensating actions, and how orchestration, choreography and two-phase commit compare.

resources.title: CQRS
resources.description: Why separating command and query models (command query responsibility segregation, CQRS) can help, why it does not require event sourcing, and when it is worth the complexity.

resources.title: Event Sourcing
resources.description: How state is derived from an immutable event history, and how snapshots and schema evolution work.

resources.title: etcd
resources.description: How etcd uses Raft consensus, watches and leases to provide a strongly consistent store for coordination.

resources.title: Polling
resources.description: How interval polling trades freshness for simplicity, and how adaptive backoff and conditional requests help it scale.

resources.title: Long Polling
resources.description: How holding a request open delivers updates sooner than polling, and how timeouts and reconnects shape the design.

resources.title: Server-Sent Events
resources.description: How a server streams one-way updates to browsers over an HTTP response (including HTTPS) with Server-Sent Events, and how reconnection, event IDs, heartbeats and proxies interact.

resources.title: WebSockets
resources.description: How the WebSocket handshake, heartbeats, authentication and cross-server fan-out work for full-duplex messaging.

resources.title: Presence
resources.description: How online status is inferred from heartbeats and TTLs, and why presence is approximate.

resources.title: Docker
resources.description: Understand image layers, container isolation and networking, and how applications are packaged and deployed consistently.

resources.title: Kubernetes
resources.description: Explore how pods, deployments, services and the control plane divide the work: the scheduler places pods, deployments manage replicas, and services give workloads stable network access.

resources.title: LLM Overview
resources.description: How text flows through tokens, transformers and next-token generation in a large language model (LLM), and which components and limits matter in applications.

resources.title: RAG Architecture
resources.description: How a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline moves from ingestion and chunking to retrieval, context assembly and citation checks.

resources.title: Vector Databases
resources.description: How vector databases store embeddings and build approximate nearest-neighbor indexes with metadata filters, and when brute force is enough.

resources.title: Model Serving
resources.description: How LLM endpoints are deployed, routed, health-checked, autoscaled and monitored, including streaming responses and canary releases.

resources.title: Retry & Backoff
resources.description: How to classify errors worth retrying and apply exponential backoff, jitter and retry budgets without overloading a recovering service.

resources.title: Circuit Breaker
resources.description: How closed, open and half-open states stop calls to a failing dependency, and how breakers differ from timeouts and fallbacks.

resources.title: Rate Limiting
resources.description: A comparison of fixed-window, sliding-window, token-bucket and leaky-bucket limiters, and what changes when limits must hold across several servers.

resources.title: Backpressure
resources.description: Learn how downstream capacity signals regulate upstream work, and compare bounded buffering, blocking and overload policies when consumers fall behind.

resources.title: Bulkhead
resources.description: How separate resource pools per workload limit the spread of resource exhaustion, so one slow dependency is less likely to consume the capacity shared by everything else.

resources.title: Load Shedding
resources.description: How rejecting low-priority work keeps a system useful under overload, and how this differs from rate limiting and circuit breaking.

resources.title: Architecture Fundamentals
resources.description: How requirements, quality attributes, constraints and assumptions combine into the decisions that define an architecture.

resources.title: Architecture Decision Making
resources.description: How to weigh options, judge how reversible a decision is, and record context and consequences in an architecture decision record.

resources.title: Scalability & Capacity
resources.description: How to find the saturated resource and choose between scaling, caching, replicas, connection pooling and sharding.

resources.title: Reliability & Resilience
resources.description: How reliability, availability and durability differ, and how service-level indicators and objectives (SLIs and SLOs) fit with resilience patterns.

resources.title: Distributed Architecture
resources.description: How partial failure, replication lag and coordination cost shape distributed designs, including CAP, quorums and consensus.

resources.title: Multi-Region Architecture
resources.description: How active-active and active-passive designs compare, what RTO and RPO mean, and when multi-region is justified over multi-AZ.

resources.title: Performance Architecture
resources.description: How to separate performance from scalability, read tail latency, and locate bottlenecks with tracing, profiling and load tests.

resources.title: Data Architecture
resources.description: Reason about data ownership, systems of record, data contracts, operational versus analytical data, and schema evolution across services.

resources.title: Platform Architecture
resources.description: Understand internal developer platforms: self-service capabilities, golden paths versus escape hatches, and the blast radius of a shared control plane.

resources.title: Architecture Evolution and Migration
resources.description: Compare incremental migration approaches such as the strangler fig, dual writes and shadowing, and plan cutover and rollback for live systems.

resources.title: Cost and Efficiency
resources.description: Evaluate fixed versus variable cost and unit economics to judge efficiency trade-offs rather than optimizing capacity in isolation.

resources.title: Security Architecture
resources.description: Treat security as an architectural decision: threat models, authentication versus authorization, service and user identity, and secrets management.

resources.title: Architecture Reviews
resources.description: How design, production-readiness, capacity and security reviews differ, and how to prioritize risks using evidence.

resources.title: Cache Stampede
resources.description: Understand why simultaneous cache misses overload a backend, and how request coalescing, TTL jitter and stale serving limit the amplification.

resources.title: Retry Storm
resources.description: How retries amplify a transient failure into an outage, and how limits, budgets and circuit breakers contain it.

resources.title: Cascading Failure
resources.description: How one slow dependency exhausts shared threads, connections and queues in the services calling it, and how timeouts and bulkheads limit the spread.

resources.title: Kafka Consumer Lag
resources.description: What makes Kafka consumers fall behind, why partition count limits how far a consumer group can scale out, and which remedies address the real bottleneck.

resources.title: Database Connection Pool Exhaustion
resources.description: How slow queries, long transactions and leaks exhaust a connection pool, and why a bigger pool can make contention worse.

resources.title: Race Condition
resources.description: See how concurrent read-modify-write operations can lose updates, and compare locking, atomic operations and optimistic concurrency as safeguards.

resources.title: Incident and Postmortem Analysis
resources.description: How to separate trigger, proximate cause, contributing factors and systemic conditions, so postmortem actions address more than one root cause.
